codeFindings.finding: Public sheet endpoint reads SQLite filename, checks local file, sets image MIME by extension plus one-day public caching and sends local file. No request-time OCR or image transformation.

previewGuide forwards remote current URL plus deduplicated cover/guide/route/pacer/live/Markdown image URLs to wx.previewImage. It does not download current image to a local temporary file or record viewer-image-ready timing; wx API success alone cannot certify a rendered original.

officialReference.observation: Official API describes current image and URL list; success/fail callbacks are call results, no documented original-image-rendered event here.

conclusion.network: These three independent public HTTP requests succeeded with correct files and normal first-byte latency. This sample did not reproduce a 10-second endpoint delay and does not establish the native-viewer network state.
conclusion.size: Each selected current image is below1MB. The full gallery passed to native preview is larger, especially Hong Kong17 images/17MB, but prefetch/decode involvement is an inference.
conclusion.rootCause: Unconfirmed. Root reproduced eventual correct native display after reopen and15-second wait. Do not classify as permanent image failure or verified network/server bug.

recommendations: Retain first loading screenshots and subsequent actual displayed screenshots; label delayed first preview honestly.
No code patch justified by the current evidence. Preserve clear originals and do not reduce fidelity merely to hide delay.

If delay recurs on a physical device, collect native network/runtime timing and compare current-image download versus viewer rendering before choosing a fix. Do not infer a server defect from wx.previewImage success or from one waiting screenshot.
A future isolated experiment could compare the same original in a one-image URL list versus its full gallery, without changing source data; it would test gallery involvement, not prove it in advance.
limitations: HTTP timings are from this workstation, not native preview instrumentation or the physical-device network.
